title: Early intervention for people living with dementia and their relatives – a feasibility study on the biopsychological evaluation of a dyadic group therapy
summary:
Dementia has profound effects on both the people living with dementia and their informal caregivers. Nevertheless, current treatment recommendations are primarily aimed either at people living with dementia or their caregivers, but usually separately from each other. In recent years, however, there has been a shift toward dyadic interventions that focus on both together.

FRIDA is a psychotherapeutic group program in which people living with dementia and their caregivers participate together. The aim is to strengthen the partnership, actively shape everyday life, and, above all, reduce stress. In 12 sessions, manual-based methods from cognitive behavioral therapy, psychosocial support, and cognitive training are combined. Central to the intervention is a focus on the couple’s resources—that is, on what they are able to manage and experience together despite the dementia. In addition to discussions about coping with dementia and the associated changes in daily life, the intervention also aims to promote pleasant shared activities, prevent social withdrawal, and maintain a relationship of equals. The program was published in 2024 and is now to be evaluated with respect to stress from a psychobiological perspective. FRIDA is therefore also investigating how stress manifests itself not only subjectively, but also in measurable physical terms – for example, via saliva or hair samples. This will enable long-term stress to be better identified and treated in a targeted manner.
conditions: People with early-stage dementia and their caregivers

interventions.name: This study is designed as a single-arm, non-randomized, prospective intervention study with a pre-post follow-up design. There is no randomization and no assignment to intervention or control groups. Caregivers and people with early-stage dementia participate together in dyadic group psychotherapy a

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Sufficient knowledge of German to understand information about the study and actively participate in group sessions and surveys
• A diagnosis of dementia (e.g., Alzheimer's dementia or other diagnosed forms)
• Ability to work in a group (the ability to integrate socially and actively participate in a structured group setting)
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute mental disorder that make participation unreasonable or impractical. These include in particular:
o Severe depressive episodes with psychotic symptoms,
o Acute suicidal tendencies or aggression towards others,
o	acute delusional disorders,
•    a Mini-Mental Status Test (MMST) score below 23 points, as in this case advanced cognitive impairment can be assumed, which significantly limits active and informed participation in the study.
